transcript:
Header: 2027-08-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 38m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Orion Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Orion Platform), Jin Park (Orion PM)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync focused on model selection, pinning strategy, fallback/rollback plans, and next-step benchmarks. Team agreed to run pinned benchmarks on rw-7b-q4 and a smaller sft variant, share logs, and provision a test VPC for end-to-end validation.

Topics: model pinning, catalog comparison, latency vs cost tradeoffs, rollback/fallback policies, security/access for Dedicated/VPC testing

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on for 30-40 minutes today. Quick roll call?
00:08 Sofia: Sofia here.
00:10 Liam: Liam here.
00:12 Jin: Jin here.
00:15 Diego: Diego from Redwood.
00:17 Maya: Great. Quick agenda — review last week's runs, dig into model selection and pinning, discuss rollback/fallbacks and security access for the VPC test. Any additions?
00:30 Sofia: No, that's good. We mostly want to understand risks around pinning to the larger rw-7b-q4 model vs using a smaller sft-7b for cost reasons.
00:45 Diego: Cool, I'll start with the perf numbers we ran yesterday. Note: some of the logs are noisy, the auto-transcript shows Q V cache as "K V cash" sometimes, so ignore weird words.
01:02 Diego: On the rw-7b-q4 we saw median token latency around 22ms on our batch size 1 runs, p95 around 85ms, p99 shot up to about 240ms for long contexts. Throughput on continuous batching improved tokens/sec by about 1.8x vs non-batched.
01:25 Sofia: Does that include prefix/KV cache warmup? Our use pattern is long conversations so cache warmup matters.
01:35 Diego: The numbers include a warmed KV cache for the primary tests; cold-starts are closer to p95 300-400ms depending on sequence length.
01:48 Jin: Are those numbers on Dedicated or Hosted? Cause we're trying to compare cost predictability.
01:55 Diego: Those were on the Dedicated staging cluster — 2xA100 equivalent. Hosted numbers were slightly higher latency and more variable.
02:08 Maya: From a product perspective, pinning to rw-7b-q4 gives better quality on our eval set. The sft-7b variant is cheaper — about 35% lower token cost — but we saw a small drop in open-ended generation quality on your catalog tests (more truncation, occasional hallucination).
02:30 Sofia: Could we do hybrid — pin the default to rw-7b-q4 for critical routes and fallback to sft-7b for lower priority workloads?
02:38 Diego: Yes, that's exactly the routing pattern Redwood supports. You can pin a model at route-level and configure a fallback chain. We recommend a canary rollout first.
02:48 Liam: On rollbacks: what's the process if we see a quality regression after a pinned update? We need a quick rollback to keep production stable.
02:56 Diego: We have automated rollbacks — if quality metrics or error rates cross thresholds, the control plane can revert to the previous model version. But the key is having good evals and thresholding. We usually recommend 5-10% canary traffic with synthetic eval prompts.
03:15 Jin: Are the thresholds configurable? We have internal SLOs for intent accuracy and latency p99.
03:21 Maya: Yes, thresholds are configurable, and the console emits token-level and per-route latency. Diego can walk through the alerting hooks.
03:30 Diego: Action-wise, I'll set up a synthetic eval with the Orion prompt set and wire it to the canary so we can auto-fail if intent accuracy drops by more than 3% or p99 latency exceeds 350ms.
03:48 Sofia: That sounds good. One security question — for the Dedicated tests, we need KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
03:58 Maya: Yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit log forwarding. We'll share the security package — apologies, it's the Redwood Dedicaded pack in the doc (transcript note: vendor name occasionally mis-typed).
04:10 Liam: On networking, we'll provision a test VPC and peering; what's the expected connectivity pattern? Do you need inbound or outbound only?
04:20 Diego: Typically outbound from the VPC to our control plane, but for private on-prem installs there's a different pattern. For the test we asked for a peering and a small NAT for metrics; we'll send a network runbook.
04:33 Sofia: Back to model selection — how do we compare catalog variants? Your catalog has rw-7b-q4, rw-7b-q8, sft-7b, and a few LLM family names that sometimes look like external names in our spreadsheet.
04:47 Diego: Right, our catalog lists performance/quality profiles. rw-7b-q4 is quantized, good latency/cost tradeoff. rw-7b-q8 is slightly cheaper but higher latencies on long contexts. The sft-7b is fine for constrained generation tasks — fewer hallucinations on slot-filling but less robust for open questions.
05:05 Jin: Are model versions stable? If we pin to rw-7b-q4 v1.3, can Redwood change the backend model under the same name?
05:12 Diego: No — when you pin you specify model and version. Our control plane won't swap versions invisibly. We do auto-update hosted defaults, but pinned routes remain fixed until you change them.
05:23 Sofia: Good. We want to pin to v1.3 for now, but we need a rollback plan to v1.2 if something goes wrong. How fast is rollback in practice?
05:31 Diego: Rollback is near-instant for routing changes — once you change the route, traffic shifts within seconds, though caches and warmup mean steady-state quality may take a minute or two.
05:45 Maya: Note: for on-prem/private, rolling versions may require a repo sync or a redeploy; that's slower. We'll flag that if you go that route.
05:56 Liam: Cost question: if we pin larger model for some routes but set routing rules to fallback to smaller ones during peak, how does billing work? Is it per actual invocation?
06:06 Maya: Billing is per-invocation and per-token. If the request hits the pinned model it bills that model's unit cost; fallback only triggers if you route it, and then you'd be billed for the model that served the request.
06:20 Sofia: For the pilot we want to compare unit economics across 2 weeks. Could Redwood provide a projected cost spreadsheet given our traffic profile?
06:28 Maya: Yes — I'll send an updated cost projection using your traffic breakdown. That's part of the pricing sheet I'll share.
06:35 Diego: Quick note on quantization: q4 gives great latency and memory savings but watch for slight reductions in numeric stability for very specific arithmetic or token-attribution tasks. For NLU classification it usually holds fine.
06:50 Jin: Any recommendations on batching or cache settings for our workload? We mostly do short queries and occasional long sessions.
06:58 Diego: For mixed short and long, set dynamic batching with a short max delay (10-20ms) and prefix caching enabled for conversation state. That typically reduces token cost by ~15% without hurting latency for short queries.
07:12 Sofia: Do you support per-customer cache isolation? We can't share KV across customers.
07:17 Diego: Yes — per-tenant KV and cache isolation. For Dedicated it's isolated by default. Hosted has tenant isolation as well.
07:25 Jin: Let's talk about the actual pinned versions we plan to test. I'm proposing: Route A (customer support NLU) pin to rw-7b-q4 v1.3; Route B (summary batch job) pin to sft-7b v2.0; Route C (low-cost fallback) to rw-7b-q8 v1.1. Thoughts?
07:45 Diego: That seems reasonable. For summaries, sft-7b v2.0 should be fine. For fallback we usually prefer smaller but compatible architecture to avoid tokenization drift — rw-7b-q8 is compatible with rw-7b-q4.
07:58 Sofia: OK we'll test that. One more concern: model drift and retraining windows — if we pin, how do we handle model improvements? We want to test new versions without breaking prod.
08:10 Maya: Use canary + staged rollout. Pin prod to v1.3, run v1.4 on 5% canary with synthetic evals and human review for 48h, then promote. If it fails we rollback.
08:22 Jin: Can we automate human review alerts? I.e., send flagged examples to our Slack channel for triage?
08:27 Diego: Yes — the console can emit failures and send webhooks; we can forward to Slack or your ticketing system.
08:34 Maya: Let's move to concrete bench tasks. Diego, can you list the exact runs you'll do?
08:40 Diego: Sure. I'll run: 1) p95/p99 latency on rw-7b-q4 v1.3 with warmed and cold cache; 2) same for sft-7b v2.0; 3) throughput under batching (batch sizes 1,4,8) to simulate your burst patterns; 4) synthetic eval for intent accuracy using the Orion prompt set. I'll upload results to the shared workbook and add notes about warmup behavior.
09:05 Sofia: Great. Will you also capture memory and GPU utilization so we can estimate Dedicated sizing?
09:11 Diego: Yes — I'll include GPU memory peaks, average utilization, and recommended node counts for your QPS.
09:18 Liam: On the VPC test: we'll aim to have peering and creds ready by Aug 24. That timeline work for Redwood?
09:25 Maya: Yes, that aligns. Diego will need access to run the end-to-end test once VPC is up.
09:31 Jin: Any outstanding legal/security gating items for the pilot? We had an open question on data retention and logs.
09:37 Maya: We'll share the SOC2 pack and a short note on retention; dedicated pilot can have shorter retention windows and we can configure log forwarding to your SIEM.
09:45 Sofia: Competitors — we also evaluated Vertex for managed endpoints; their price was lower for some configs but we liked Redwood's routing and rollback tooling better.
09:56 Diego: Thanks. We'll send a short comparison note (not exhaustive) highlighting rollback, canary, and per-route pinning features.
10:04 Maya: Quick time check — about 25 minutes in. Any other risks we haven't covered?
10:10 Sofia: One more thing: tokenization differences across models could cause slight intent mismatches. How do you recommend validating?
10:17 Diego: We recommend a side-by-side evaluation using your prompts and normalized tokenization metrics; I'll include a token-diff column in the benchmark sheet.
10:26 Jin: Perfect.
10:28 Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send pricing and the Dedicated quote; Diego will run benchmarks and upload; Sofia/Liam will provision VPC and share logs; Jin will confirm eval metrics. We'll run a rollback tabletop on Aug 27.
10:45 Sofia: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
10:49 Maya: Thanks all. Bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and run-on lines, speaker attribution approximated. Links referenced during call: Pricing sheet (link shared in chat), Security pack (link), Shared benchmark workbook (link).
